(Capacity: 13,819) |champion= |tourney= |tourney_result= }} {{2018–19 Pac-12 Conference men's basketball standings}} The '''2018–19 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team''' represented the [[University of California, Los Angeles]] during the [[2018–19 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|Bruins]] played their home games at [[Pauley Pavilion]] as members in the [[Pac-12 Conference]]. They were led by sixth-year head coach [[Steve Alford]] until he was fired mid-season and assistant [[Murry Bartow]] was named the interim head coach.{{Cite web|url=https://uclabruins.com/news/2018/12/31/mens-basketball-ucla-head-coach-steve-alford-relieved-of-duties.aspx|title = UCLA Head Coach Steve Alford Relieved of Duties}} Their lineup featured three former [[McDonald's All-American]]s: sophomores [[Jaylen Hands]] and [[Kris Wilkes]] were both named second-team [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-12]], while first-year player [[Moses Brown (basketball)|Moses Brown]] was voted to the Pac-12 All-Freshman Team.{{cite news|last=Nguyen|first=Thuc Nhi|title=UCLA's Jaylen Hands, Kris Wilkes named All-Pac-12 second team|date=March 11, 2019|newspaper=Los Angeles Daily News|url=https://www.dailynews.com/2019/03/11/uclas-jaylen-hands-kris-wilkes-named-all-pac-12-second-team/|access-date=March 12, 2019}} UCLA finished the season 17–16, and lost in the second round of the [[2019 Pac-12 Conference men's basketball tournament|Pac-12 tournament]]. They missed the postseason for the second time in four years.{{cite news|last=Nguyen|first=Thuc Nhi|title=UCLA men's basketball kept out of postseason tournaments on Selection Sunday|date=March 17, 2019|newspaper=Los Angeles Daily News|url=https://www.dailynews.com/2019/03/17/ucla-mens-basketball-kept-out-of-postseason-tournaments-on-selection-sunday/|access-date=March 20, 2019}} Ranked No. 21 in the preseason [[AP Poll]], the Bruins began the season 4–0 and climbed to No. 17.{{cite news|title=Steve Alford's UCLA run ends with Liberty rock bottom|date=December 31, 2018|newspaper=New York Post|url=https://nypost.com/2018/12/31/steve-alfords-ucla-run-ends-with-liberty-rockbottom/|access-date=December 31, 2018}} However, they lost six of the next nine and finished with a 7–6 record in nonconference play, closing it out with four straight losses, the last of which was a 73–58 defeat to [[2018–19 Liberty Flames basketball team|Liberty]]. They committed a season-high 24 [[turnover (basketball)|turnovers]] in the game,{{cite news|last=Bolch|first=Ben|title=UCLA's sloppy play leads to 69-55 loss at Washington|date=February 2, 2019|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/la-sp-ucla-washington-20190202-story.html|access-date=February 7, 2019}} and the 15-point setback was the most lopsided home loss in Alford's tenure with UCLA.{{cite news|last=Bolch|first=Ben|title=UCLA suffers disappointing 73-58 loss to Liberty, the Bruins' fourth straight defeat|date=December 29, 2018|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/la-sp-ucla-liberty-20181229-story.html|access-date=December 29, 2018}} Combined with an earlier home loss to [[mid-major]] program [[2018–19 Belmont Bruins men's basketball team|Belmont]], it was the first time the Bruins had lost consecutive home games to non-[[Power Five]] schools since [[2012–13 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|2012–13]].{{cite news|title=Liberty extends UCLA's woes with 73-58 victory|date=December 29, 2018|website=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401087154|access-date=December 29, 2018}} Four days after Belmont, they lost by 29 at [[2018–19 Cincinnati Bearcats men's basketball team|Cincinnati]], their largest margin of defeat since [[2014–15 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|2014–15]]. UCLA had not lost four straight since the end of [[2015–16 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|2015–16]], when they finished the season under .500.{{cite news|last=Kaufman|first=Joey|title=UCLA falls to Liberty, closing non-conference play with fourth straight loss|date=December 29, 2018|newspaper=Orange County Register|url=https://www.ocregister.com/2018/12/29/ucla-falls-to-liberty-closing-non-conference-play-with-fourth-straight-loss/|access-date=December 29, 2018}} They had not suffered four consecutive nonconference losses since [[2010–11 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|2010–11]].{{cite news|title=Pac-12 caps worst December by major conference in 20 years as five teams lose|date=December 29, 2018|website=ESPN.com|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/25641970/pac-12-caps-worst-december-major-conference-20-years-five-teams-lose|access-date=December 30, 2018}} On December 31, 2018, two days after the Bruins' loss to Liberty, UCLA fired Alford and named Bartow the interim head coach. The Bruins were inconsistent under Bartow, logging as many three-game winning streaks as three-game losing streaks. They opened conference play 2–0 at home against [[San Francisco Bay Area]] schools [[2018–19 Stanford Cardinal men's basketball team|Stanford]] and [[2018–19 California Golden Bears men's basketball team|California]].{{cite news|last=Bennett|first=Brain|title=Bennett on basketball: Bartow doubles down in attempt to turn UCLA's season around|date=January 7, 2019|publisher=Bay Area News Group|url=https://www.mercurynews.com/2019/01/07/bennett-on-basketball-bartow-doubles-down-in-attempt-to-turn-uclas-season-around/|access-date=January 7, 2019}} Emphasizing the team's speed and athleticism, he had the Bruins play more aggressive, trapping and applying pressure on defense and attacking on offense by running on both missed and made baskets. Six Bruins scored in double figures against Cal after five reached the threshold against the Cardinal. In their 13 non-conference games under Alford, UCLA never had more than four double-figure scorers.{{cite news|last=Bolch|first=Ben|title=UCLA relies on faster tempo and more pressure to rout California|date=January 5, 2019|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/la-sp-ucla-california-20190105-story.html|access-date=January 6, 2019}}{{cite news|last=Nguyen|first=Thuc Nhi|title=A men's basketball takes team-first attitude to beat Cal|date=January 5, 2019|newspaper=Los Angeles Daily News|url=https://www.dailynews.com/2019/01/05/ucla-mens-basketball-uses-defense-to-offset-sloppiness-and-beat-cal/|access-date=January 6, 2019}} The Bruins won the following game in overtime 87–84 at [[2018–19 Oregon Ducks men's basketball team|Oregon]] after rallying from 17 points down with less than seven minutes left in the second half, and later trailing by nine with 51 seconds remaining. It was the largest comeback in the final minute of a Pac-12 game and tied the sixth-largest deficit overcome in the last minute in [[NCAA Division I|Division I]] history. UCLA's 3–0 start in the conference was their best since starting 5–0 in the Pac-12 in [[2012–13 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|2012–13]], the last time they claimed a conference regular-season title.{{cite news|last=Bolch|first=Ben|title=UCLA battles back for an improbable road win over Oregon|date=January 10, 2019|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/la-sp-ucla-oregon-20190110-story.html|access-date=January 22, 2019}} However, they lost their next three games, falling to 3–7 in their last 10, and 10–9 overall.{{cite news|last=Nguyen|first=Thuc Nhi|title=UCLA men's basketball fades against Arizona State for third straight loss|date=January 24, 2019|newspaper=Los Angeles Daily News|url=https://www.dailynews.com/2019/01/24/ucla-mens-basketball-fades-against-arizona-state-for-third-straight-loss/|access-date=February 7, 2019}} After wins over [[2018–19 Arizona Wildcats men's basketball team|Arizona]] and [[2018–19 Washington State Cougars men's basketball team|Washington State]], during which they set season-highs in [[field goal percentage]] of 57.9 and 58.8 percent, respectively,{{cite news|last=Nguyen|first=Thuc Nhi|title=UCLA men's basketball gets major test at first-place Washington|date=February 1, 2019|newspaper=Los Angeles Daily News|url=https://www.dailynews.com/2019/02/01/ucla-mens-basketball-gets-major-test-at-first-place-washington/|access-date=February 7, 2019}} they lost to [[2018–19 Washington Huskies men's basketball team|Washington]] after committing 23 turnovers.{{cite news|last=Nguyen|first=Thuc Nhi|title=Halfway through Pac-12 play, UCLA men's basketball is well out of NCAA picture|date=February 5, 2019|newspaper=Los Angeles Daily News|url=https://www.dailynews.com/2019/02/05/halfway-through-pac-12-season-ucla-mens-basketball-well-out-of-ncaa-picture/|access-date=February 7, 2019}} The Bruins were 5–4 halfway through the conference schedule. While Bartow was pushing for a faster pace, an unintended consequence was UCLA's conference-leading 17.3 turnovers per game, almost four more than they committed during non-conference play. Entering the second half, UCLA had a favorable schedule with seven of their last nine regular-season games against schools that were ranked in the bottom half of the Pac-12. However, they lost their third straight game on February 9 after blowing a 22-point lead with 12:10 remaining in a 93–92 loss to [[2018–19 Utah Utes men's basketball team|Utah]], which won on a buzzer-beating [[three-point field goal]]. The Bruins allowed 61 points in the second half, the most they had surrendered in a half since allowing 64 points in a win against [[Cal State Northridge Matadors men's basketball|Cal State Northridge]] in [[1998–99 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|1998]]. The Bruins dropped into a four-way tie for seventh place in the Pac-12.{{cite news|last=Nguyen|first=Thuc Nhi|title=UCLA men's basketball resets after crushing collapse against Utah|date=February 12, 2019|newspaper=Los Angeles Daily News|url=https://www.dailynews.com/2019/02/12/ucla-mens-basketball-resets-after-crushing-collapse-against-utah/|access-date=February 16, 2019}} Combined with a loss earlier in the week to [[2018–19 Colorado Buffaloes men's basketball team|Colorado]], it was the first time that UCLA had been swept in a home series since [[2015–16 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|2015–16]].{{cite news|last=Nguyen|first=Thuc Nhi|title=UCLA blows 22-point lead as Utah wins on 3-pointer at the buzzer|date=February 9, 2019|newspaper=Los Angeles Daily News|url=https://www.dailynews.com/2019/02/09/ucla-blows-22-point-lead-as-utah-wins-on-3-pointer-at-the-buzzer/|access-date=February 10, 2019}} However, UCLA won four of their next five. The four wins consisted of two overtime games, a one-point victory, and a 19-point comeback.{{cite news|last=Nguyen|first=Thuc Nhi|title=UCLA men's basketball thrives on strong connection during late-season run|date=March 1, 2019|newspaper=Los Angeles Daily News|url=https://www.dailynews.com/2019/03/01/ucla-mens-basketball-thrives-on-strong-connection-during-late-season-run/|access-date=March 3, 2019}} They entered the final week of the regular season with a chance to finish as high as third place in the conference, but lost their final two games to fall to seventh.{{cite news|last=Nguyen|first=Thuc Nhi|title=UCLA men's basketball finishes seventh in Pac-12 after loss to Utah|date=March 9, 2019|newspaper=Los Angeles Daily News|url=https://www.dailynews.com/2019/03/09/ucla-mens-basketball-finishes-seventh-in-pac-12-after-loss-to-utah/|access-date=March 11, 2019}} In their opening game of the [[2019 Pac-12 Conference men's basketball tournament|Pac-12 tournament]], UCLA switched to a [[man-to-man defense]] after having played predominantly [[zone defense|zone]] under Bartow, and they defeated Stanford 79–72. Bruins freshman guard David Singleton broke his foot in the final minute, ending his season.{{cite news|last=Bolch|first=Ben|title=Jaylen Hands helps UCLA hold off Stanford rally in Pac-12 tournament victory|date=March 13, 2019|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/la-sp-ucla-stanford-20190313-story.html|access-date=March 14, 2019}} The Bruins lost their next game 83–72 to second-seeded [[2018–19 Arizona State Sun Devils men's basketball team|Arizona State]] in the quarterfinals. They were down by two points with 3:59 remaining before halftime. However, they were outscored 14–0 to end the half, and trailed by double-digits throughout most of the rest of the game.{{cite news|last=Kaufman|first=Joey|title=UCLA falls to Arizona State in Pac-12 Tournament quarterfinals|date=March 15, 2019|newspaper=Orange County Register|url=https://www.dailynews.com/2019/03/14/ucla-falls-to-arizona-state-in-pac-12-tournament-quarterfinals/|access-date=March 16, 2019}}{{cite news|last=Bolch|first=Ben|title=UCLA can't overcome sluggish first half in 83-72 loss to Arizona State in Pac-12 quarterfinals|date=March 14, 2019|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/la-sp-ucla-arizona-state-20190314-story.html|access-date=March 16, 2019}} Afterwards, Bartow stated that he was not interested in having his interim tag removed, and expressed optimism that UCLA would "hire a very good coach". ==Previous season== {{main|2017–18 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team}} The Bruins finished the 2017–18 season 21–12, 11–7 in Pac-12 play to finish in a three-way tie for third place. They defeated [[2017–18 Stanford Cardinal men's basketball team|Stanford]] in the quarterfinals of the [[2018 Pac-12 Conference men's basketball tournament|Pac-12 tournament]] to advance to the semifinals where they lost to [[2017–18 Arizona Wildcats men's basketball team|Arizona]].
